newsitem.title: CANADA: Talisman's bid for Wascana seen hard to top.
newsitem.headline: Talisman's bid for Wascana seen hard to top.

text.p: Talisman Energy Inc.'s C$1.7 billion ($1.3 billion) takeover bid for Wascana Energy Inc. is expected to be hard to top, but analysts are not ruling out a competing offer.

Talisman, one of Canada's largest independent oil and gas producers, with worldwide operations, said late on Wednesday it would offer C$18.50 cash ($13.70) or 0.41 of one of its shares for each share of Wascana, a former Saskatchewan government-owned oil company.
Wascana said in a terse statement on Thursday it would review the bid.
Talisman Chief Executive Jim Buckee has completed several large acquisitions since 1992 and is viewed as one of the Canadian energy industry's shrewdest bidders.
"When he goes after something, he wins," said Matt Janisch, analyst with brokerage Nesbitt Burns in Calgary.
"He's done other acquisitions that the market has questioned, but his track record in showing value through acquisitions has been very good," Janisch said.

Despite Talisman's record of deals, analysts said Wascana's future was not sealed and that several Canadian firms with complementary operations to Wascana's Saskatchewan heavy oil business were potential rival bidders.

Industry sources said the list included Alberta Energy Co. Ltd., Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd., Norcen Energy Resources Ltd., Canadian Natural Resources Ltd., PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd., plus long shots Petro-Canada and Suncor Inc..
Wascana could also hold interest for a U.S.-based firm, sources said.
"Certainly lots of companies had files on Wascana," First Energy Capital Corp. analyst Martin Molyneaux said. "I wouldn't be surprised if somebody comes out of the woodwork."

Buckee said in a conference call on Thursday that Talisman was one of a "very limited" list of potential Wascana acquirers because of the deal's size, the two firms' extensive operational overlap and the need for a bid to be acceptable to the Saskatchewan government.
Talisman said 40 percent of Wascana shares would be acquired for cash and the rest swapped for Talisman stock.
The offer would also include the assumption of about C$200 million ($148 million) in long-term debt.
The Saskatchewan government, which late last year scrapped a rule that no single shareholder could own more than 10 percent of the company, holds 7.3 percent of Wascana shares.

Berny Wiens, Saskatchewan's Minister of Crown Investments Corp., told Reuters that Talisman's moves appeared to fit his government's economic objectives, which included establishing the western Canadian province as a center for heavy oil expertise.
Wiens said no decision on tendering the government's shares to the offer had been made.
Wascana shares, the Toronto Stock Exchange's most active issue on Thursday, closed up C$2.05 to C$19, about the same level as the share exchange value of the Talisman offer.
"The market right now is saying, 'Done,'" analyst Janisch said.
Talisman shares closed up C$1.10 to C$46.25 in Toronto.
